pubflow

{pubflow} (“publishing workflow”) is the companion package of pipeflow (>= 0.5.0.9032): it takes the results a pipeline computes and covers what is needed to publish them.

Why pubflow?

Unlike knitr, rmarkdown and Quarto, a pubflow document is not a source file to knit: the pipeline builds it, so it can update in place and feed a viewer or a report.

  • Parameter UI for free: Shiny inputs and validation built from a pipeline’s params
  • Live preview: see a change in the viewer without re-knitting the document
  • Only what changed: documents are pipeline steps, so pipeflow re-runs just what a change affects
  • Same document, every format: the same tables, figures and text in HTML, Word, PDF and Markdown
  • Traceable by design: deterministic output with trace stamps and session info

Status

Under development towards v0.1. The design is in dev/DESIGN.md, the open work in dev/PLAN.md.

Installation 

# Install development version from GitHub
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("rpahl/pubflow")

Usage

A step returns a table, a layout step arranges it into a document, and pub_render() writes the document to a file:

library(pipeflow)
library(pubflow)

pip <- pip_new("my-pip") |>
    pip_add("fit", function(data = airquality, xVar = "Temp") {
        coefs <- coef(lm(paste("Ozone ~", xVar), data = data))
        data.frame(term = names(coefs), estimate = unname(coefs))
    }) |>
    pip_add("table", function(fit = ~fit) {
        pub_table(fit, caption = "Linear model of the ozone concentration")
    }) |>
    pip_add("report", function(table = ~table) {
        pub_doc(pub_section("Results", table), title = "Ozone in New York")
    })
pip_run(pip)
pub_render(pip[["report", "out"]], "html")
pub_render(pip[["report", "out"]], "md")

Learning pubflow

If you are new to pubflow, read the vignettes in the order they are listed below. They build one example up from a pipeline with params to a report file and a Shiny app.
